summary: Adds a thumbnail helper that shells out to ImageMagick convert, a docs URL setting, and a GET /calc endpoint that evaluates an arithmetic expression.

findings.title: Request query evaluated as JavaScript
findings.problem: The /calc handler passes req.query.expr straight to eval. The added comments switch off the lint checks that would report this line.
findings.consequence: Any caller of /calc can run arbitrary JavaScript inside the server process. That caller can read secrets, touch files and spawn processes.
findings.fix: Parse expr with a restricted arithmetic evaluator such as expr-eval, or with a small hand-written parser. Remove the disable comments.

findings.title: Shell command built from upload name
findings.problem: make_thumbnail puts upload_name into a shell command string and runs it with shell=True. Its docstring says the upload form supplies the name.
findings.consequence: A user who uploads a file named with shell metacharacters runs commands on the server. A name containing ../ also writes outside THUMB_DIR.
findings.fix: Pass an argument list to subprocess.run without shell=True. Reject names that are not a plain basename.

findings.title: New code paths have no covering test
findings.problem: This change adds make_thumbnail and the /calc route without any tests. No test covers the new behaviour.
findings.consequence: A regression in input handling for either path goes unnoticed. That matters more because both paths handle untrusted input.
findings.fix: Add tests that call make_thumbnail and /calc with normal and hostile inputs.

dropped.reason: The noqa covers only the line length of a long documentation URL constant. It hides no real problem.
The nosec hides the same shell injection that the finding on this line already raises.
The disable comment hides the eval injection that the finding on line 12 already raises.
The nosemgrep comment hides the eval injection that the finding on this line already raises.
Importing subprocess is not a problem by itself. The unsafe call on line 9 is raised separately.
